Mr. S.C. Das with Mr. Rabi Shankar Chakraborty, Advocates --------- for the Petitioner
Mr. H.S. Deb Brahman with Mr. S.M. Asadullah, Advocates ----------- for the opposite party
parties:
Sree Sree Narayan Chakra Bigraha ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Niranjan Bhattacharjee ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md. Hamidul Haque, J: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree passed in Other Appeal No. 211/85 by the learned Subordinate Judge, Patiya dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree passed in Other Suit No. 266/83 by the learned Munsif, Patiya dismissing the suit.

2. The present petitioner as Shebayet of dioty Sree Sree Narayan Chandra Bigraha filed the above suit for a decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. The plaintiff claims that the suit land belonged Banga Chandra Bhattachery who dedicated the same infavour of the dioty by executing a will on 3rd Chaitra 1284 Mghi Era. Banga Chandra appointed his wife Shama Sundari and one of his sons Nara Hari as executors. It was stated in the will itself that his eldest son Brojahari was in different and callous and as such he was not made an executor. Another condition laid down in the will was that his sons and female members of the family who would not reside in the homestead would not be entitled to get any “prashad”. Further case of the plaintiff is that l3rojahara and his son the defendant No. 1 left the homestead and not resides in that homestead nor performed any puja of the deity. Next he claimed that after death of Norahari one of executor of the will be filed a probate case and got the probate and since then he has been performing puja and other religious rites but the defendant No. 1 threatened his to dispossess from the suit land on 27.6.96 hence the suit.

3. Defendant no. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement admitting that the suit property belonged to Bhanga Hari Bhattacharjee but claimed that Bhanga Hari never executed any will claimed by the plaintiff.

4. He claimed that his father Broja Hari was a normal man and resided in the homestead and also died there. He also claimed that he had possessed the suit property in ejmali with the plaintiff and Sudhangshu Bala widow of Narahari Bhattacharijee. According to him Norahari was as scholar in sanskrit and used to run a Sanakrit tole in the suit homestead and the plaintiff was a teacher in the tole and he established a deity in his own house and had been performing puja of that deity. The defdt also contended that the suit was not maintainable in the present form.

5. The learned Munsif dismissed the suit on the ground that the defendant proved his ejmali possession in the suit land. The plaintiff then preferred the above appeal. The appellate court also concurred with the findings of the trial court and dismissed the appeal. The plaintiff then preferred the present application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

6. In the grounds it is stated that the courts below committed an error of law in not appreciating the oral evidence and the will and other documents filed by the plaintiff.

<u>7. It is admitted that the suit property belonged to Banga Chandra Bhattacharjee and he left behind 3 sons Brojahari, Norahari and Haripada (the shebeyat who filed the suit). The plaintiff claims that Banga Chandra executed a will in respect of his entire immovable property and dedicated the same to the deity Sree Sree Narayan Chakra Bigharaha. The defendant on the other hand claims that Banga Chandra never executed such a will. It appears that the plaintiff by filing a case got the probate and that has been filed and marked exhibit 2. The defendant claims that the probate was obtained behind his back. While the defendant deposed as D.W. 1 a suggestion was given to him to the effect that he filed a case for revocation of the probate then he admitted that he filed case No. 77/77 and that case was dismissed for default. In view of the above admission the defendant now cannot challenge the probate granted to the plaintiff. Grant of a probate is the proof of validity of a will. So, after granting of probate and after disposal of the revocation caw filed by the defendant there is no scope for determining whether Banga Chandra executed a will or not.</u>

8. The learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite party has contended that the will was created by the Shebayet Hari Pada and in this regard he referred to the statement of P.W. 1 in his examination in-chief where he stated that his father Banga Chandra died on 2nd Jaishta 1284 Maghia ers. So according to him if Banga Chandra died on 2nd Jaistha, 1284 Maghi era, the execution of the will by Banga Chandra on 3rd Chaitra 1284 Maghi era can never be believed. It appears that actually D.W. 1 gave the date of his father death as 2nd Jaistha 1284 Maghi era, but the question of genuineness or validity of the will as I have mentioned earlier cannot be determined in this suit as already probate was granted in a formal proceeding by a competent court.

9. Now, it appears that the suit being a suit for permanent injunction the question of Possession is the most important question which requires decision. In this regard the cast of the plaintiff is that in view of the condition laid down in the will be Brojahari did not reside in the homestead he was not entitled to enjoy "Proshadi". The plaintiff's further case is that son of Brajahari that is the contesting defendant also never resided in the homestead plot and as such he is not entitled to enjoy proshed or the property dedicated to the deity. The defendant, on the other hand, claims that his father used to reside in the homestead plot and also died there. Both the courts on the basis of the evidence on record believed the case of the defendant in this regard.

10. The plaintiff, in view of a recital in the will, claims that Brajahari was indifferent and callous type of man and as such he was not appointed executor though he was the eldest son of Banga Chandra. It appears to me that the question whether Brojahari was indifferent or callous type of man or a normal man is not very much relevant for the purpose of arriving at a decision in this suit. The relevant question is whether Brojahari left the homestead of his father or used to reside on that homestead. The will executed on 3rd Chaitra, 1284 Maghi era which corresponds to 1924 A.D. There is no evidence to show in which year Banga Chandra died except the statement of D.W.1 as referred to earlier. Now, from exhibits 6 and 6(a) it appears that the property was recorded in R.S. Khatians in the names of three sons of Banga Chandra in equal shares and not in the names of the deity. These khatiana were finally published in the year 1930. The plaintiff did not claim that the khatians were wrong. That means these khatians remained unchallenged. In these khatinas 3/1rd shares has been recorded in the name of Brojahari and as such it cannot be said that Brojahari left the locality. The D.W.1 in his cross-examination said that the marriage ceremony of Brojahari was held in his father's house. P.W. 5 who is 75 years old stated that Brojahari was known to him and he used to reside in the suit homestead and also died there. This is exactly the case of the contesting defendant. It is definite case of the contesting defendent that his father used to reside in the suit homestead and died there. In view of R.S. khatians and the statements of the P.W.1 and P.W. 5 as mentioned above it is quite clear the Brojahari used to reside in the homestead plot of his father till his death. So, there is no truth in the claim of the plaintiff that Brojahari had no right to enjoy the proshadi in view of the condition laid down in the will because he did not reside in the homestead of Banga Chandra.

11. The next question is whether the defendant can be restrained from enjoying the proshadi or the suit property. Condition No. 4 as liad down in the will is as follows:

আমার পুত্রগন ও স্ত্রিয়া লোকগনের মধ্যে যিনি আমার বাড়ীতে বসতী করিবেন না তিনি ঠাকুর সেবার কোন প্রসাদি পাইবেন না এবং বাটাস্থ সেবাকারী স্ত্রিয়া লোক ভিন্ন প্রসাদি ভোগের অন্য কাহারো স্বত্ব বর্তিবেক না।

12. From this condition it is clear that the sons and the female members who would not reside in the homestead would not get any proshadi. We have found that Brojahari son of Banga Chandra used to reside in the homestead of his father and also died there. Restrictions imposed under condition no. 4 is in respect of the sons of Banga Chandra. So, even if the defendant No. 1 who his grandson of Banga Chandra does not reside permanently in the parental homestead he cannot be restrained from enjoying the property.

13. In view of my discussion above I am of the opinion that the plaintiff is not entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction against the defendant and as such I find no reason to interfere with the decisions of the courts below.

14. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. Send down the L.C.R. atone.

End.
